findings.summary: The page uses ESP, initramfs and "dracut shell" before any of them is defined; the debug rule leans on them.
findings.evidence: "Reads | MBR: first 512 bytes of the disk | .efi files from the ESP" and "a kernel panic or dracut shell means kernel or initramfs"
findings.fix: Expand ESP as EFI System Partition on first use. Add one line to the boot-order diagram saying initramfs is a temporary root in RAM holding the drivers needed to mount the real root. Say that dracut is the initramfs tool whose emergency shell appears when root cannot be mounted, with a pointer to page 3.

findings.summary: Code block is shown with a mixed-distro comment and a trailing explanatory line, so the RHEL UEFI path caveat is buried in a code comment.
findings.evidence:
# UEFI on RHEL 8 or older: -o /boot/efi/EFI/redhat/grub.cfg
first: Debian/Ubuntu, second: RHEL
findings.fix: Present the commands as a Distro | Command table (Debian/Ubuntu, RHEL BIOS, RHEL 8 UEFI) like the initramfs table on page 3.

findings.summary: The BIOS vs UEFI comparison table is repeated almost entirely from page 1 with different rows, so the same comparison is split across two pages.
findings.evidence: Page 1: "ESP format | none | FAT32" and "Reads | MBR: first 512 bytes of the disk | .efi files from the ESP"; Page 2: "Disk layout | MBR | GPT + ESP"
findings.fix: Merge into one BIOS vs UEFI table on one page and reference it from the other.

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "arguments", "running").
findings.evidence: View the arguments the running kernel got: cat /proc/cmdline (e.g. root=UUID=... ro quiet)
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: A bullet holds two ideas: file name per distro plus a definition of initrd, and the vmlinuz bullet is a different idea on the same level.
findings.fix: Split into a small table: File | Role | Debian/Ubuntu name | RHEL name.

findings.summary: Several bullets carry multiple ideas and the logs table mixes commands with '=' style bullets for the same kind of fact.
findings.evidence: "systemd is PID 1, the ancestor of all userspace processes" and "systemd-analyze blame = slowest units" listed as bullets under a Command | Shows table
findings.fix: Put systemd-analyze, systemd-analyze blame and systemctl --failed as rows in the Command | Shows table, and split the PID 1 bullet.

findings.summary: The Load/Unload bullet list mixes three separate topics (persist, blacklist, remove-guard) with no grouping.
findings.evidence: "Load at boot: /etc/modules-load.d/*.conf" / "Stop auto-loading a driver: blacklist <mod> in /etc/modprobe.d/*.conf" / "A module with non-zero used-by cannot be removed"
findings.fix: Add a small Goal | Where table for persist/blacklist and move the used-by rule next to the lsmod bullet.
